findings.title: from_f64_with_unit/from_f32_with_unit return 0 bytes for tiny positive sizes instead of rounding up
findings.property: A positive size is rounded up to at least 1 byte, and from_f64_with_unit(x, Unit::B) equals from_f64(x)
findings.evidence: Docs: 'The calculated byte will be rounded up.' from_f64 documents 'The fractional part will be rounded up' and returns 1 for 1e-29. The Decimal conversion (Decimal::from_f64) silently flattens values below 1e-28 to zero before the ceil.

review.title: from_f64_with_unit/from_f32_with_unit return Byte(0) for positive sizes below 1e-28, unlike from_f64/from_f32
review.reason: Both functions document 'The calculated byte will be rounded up', and Byte::from_f64(1e-29) returns Byte(1) via ceil. The _with_unit variants first convert through rust_decimal's Decimal::from_f64, which cannot represent values below 1e-28 and returns zero. A positive size therefore becomes Byte(0), and the same input gives different results depending on the entry point. The input is valid (>= 0) and the repro uses the API correctly. The case is extremely obscure, and a maintainer could treat it as a limit of the Decimal dependency. A small clamp (positive input with a zero result becomes 1) would fix it.
